provenance.l: Apollo 15 Mission Report MSC-05161 (Dec 1971): Table 3-III, entry interface 294:58:54.7 at 400,000 ft, 36,096.4 ft/s (11,002 m/s), flight-path angle -6.51 deg, 14.23 N 175.02 E; Table A-III, command module weight at entry 12,953 lb (5,875 kg; OCR of the table, the CM after separation reads 12,965); section 6.1, main parachute deployment "beginning at approximately 10 500 feet" (9.13 pilot report: 10 000 feet); Table 3-I drogues 295:06:46, mains 295:07:34, landing "a safe landing was made at 295:11:53" (20:45:53 GMT 7 August 1971) at 26 deg 7.8 min N, 158 deg 8.4 min W (computer), about 1 n.mi from the target, USS Okinawa. Quote: "One of the three main parachutes was deflated to approximately one-fifth of its full diameter at about 6000 feet altitude. The command module descended in this configuration to landing." (section 14.1.9): the landing came about 32 seconds earlier than on three mains; the physics here flies three mains (one fixed terminal CdA), the deflated canopy is drawn only

NASA SP-4029 Apollo chronology, "Entry, Splashdown, and Recovery" compilation (Apollo 7-17): Apollo 15 column: "Lift To Drag Ratio 0.290", "Range (n mi) 1,184" (1,184 n.mi = 2,193 km), "Maximum g 6.23", "Duration (sec) 778.3", velocity 36,096.4 ft/s, flight-path angle -6.51, splashdown 26.13 N 158.13 W, landing weight 11,731 lb. No Entry Postflight Analysis exists for Apollo 15 (the mission report's supplement list has none), so L/D and range are the compilation values (secondary), not a reconstruction; no first/second load-factor split is published. Model limit (US Standard Atmosphere 1976, 2026-11-25): with these inputs the model's first pulse is 6.6 g at 81 s (6.23 g flown), it dips to 2 g, second pulse 6.6 g; drogues 417 s (471 s flown, 295:06:46), splashdown 783 s (778 s flown; the flown figure is with one main deflated, which landed it about 32 s earlier than three mains, so about 810 s on three). The larger pulse is within 10% of the flown maximum g; the entry runs short of the flown time, a limit of the fixed-bank planar guidance (on Apollo 11, the one flight with a published minimum, it lofts to 0.8 g between the pulses against the flown 0.48 g)
Apollo CM entry aero (L/D 0.3), drogue and main areas: the Apollo 8 profile (MSC-PA-R-69-1), same Block II command module
